nodes.name: Electrochemical Deposition of Ni Nanocones
nodes.procedure: Electrochemical deposition was performed on pretreated nickel foam (NF) substrate. The pristine NF exhibits a smooth surface (Figure S1). Optimal conditions: electrodeposition time of 8 min at current density of 20 mA·cm⁻², yielding well-defined conical Ni structures that serve as scaffolds for subsequent hydrothermal growth.

unit_operations.name: Electrochemical Deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Electrochemical deposition led to the formation of conical Ni structures on the NF substrate (Figure S2)

nodes.source_text: Figure 1a shows... The self-supporting electrode, featuring a hierarchical nanocone-nanoneedle structure, was synthesized via a two-step process consisting of electrochemical deposition followed by hydrothermal treatment on pretreated NF. As shown in Figure S1 (Supporting Information), the pristine NF exhibits a smooth surface. Electrochemical deposition led to the formation of conical Ni structures on the NF substrate (Figure S2, Supporting Information)

nodes.name: Hydrothermal Growth of CoFe2O4 Nanoneedles
nodes.procedure: Dense, needle-like CoFe2O4 features were grown hydrothermally on the Ni/NF nanocone scaffolds obtained from step 1. Optimal conditions: 120°C for 8 h, yielding uniform ultrathin nanoneedles anchored on nanocone substrate, forming the final hierarchical Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode (Figure 1e; Figure S3).

unit_operations.name: Hydrothermal Reaction
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: hydrothermal growth of dense, needle-like CoFe2O4 features, yielding the final hierarchical Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode

nodes.source_text: which subsequently served as scaffolds for the hydrothermal growth of dense, needle-like CoFe2O4 features, yielding the final hierarchical Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode (Figure 1e; Figure S3, Supporting Information)... The optimal conditions (120°C for 8 h) yielded a dense array of ultrathin nanoneedles

nodes.name: Annealing to Remove Hierarchical Structure
nodes.procedure: The Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode was annealed at 800°C to remove the nanocone-nanoneedle features while maintaining identical chemical composition, producing the control sample Ni-CoFe2O4/NF-800.

unit_operations.name: Annealing
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: by annealing the Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode at 800°C to remove the nanocone-nanoneedle features

nodes.source_text: a control sample (Ni-CoFe2O4/NF-800) with identical chemical composition but lacking the hierarchical structure was also prepared by annealing the Ni-CoFe2O4/NF electrode at 800°C

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacings of 2.5 Å and 2.9 Å corresponding to the (311) and (200) planes of CoFe₂O₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) revealed lattice spacings of 2.5 Å and 2.9 Å, corresponding to the (311) and (200) planes of CoFe₂O₄ (Figure S20, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows reflections at 2θ = 30.0°, 35.4°, 62.5° for (220), (311), (440) planes of CoFe₂O₄ and 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.3° for (111), (200), (220) planes of metallic Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of Ni-CoFe₂O₄/NF showed reflections at 2θ = 30.0°, 35.4°, and 62.5°, corresponding to the (220), (311), and (440) planes of CoFe₂O₄ along with additional reflections at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.3° indexed to the (111), (200), and (220) planes of metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS element mapping confirms homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and Co within the nanoneedles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) element mapping confirmed a homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and Co within the nanoneedles.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms Ni, Co, Fe, O presence. Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺/Ni³⁺ with 0.4 eV positive shift in Ni³⁺. Fe 2p shows Fe²⁺ (709.8, 723.9 eV), Fe³⁺ (714.2, 726.6 eV) with 0.7 eV shift. Co 2p shows Co²⁺/Co³⁺ with 0.9 eV shift. O 1s: lattice O (531.9 eV), M-OH (533.2 eV), H₂O (534.3 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectra confirm the presence of Ni, Co, Fe, and O... The O 1s spectrum of Ni-CoFe₂O₄/NF shows three well-resolved components: lattice oxygen (M-O, 531.9 eV), surface hydroxyls (M-OH, 533.2 eV), and adsorbed H₂O (534.3 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman monitoring under OER conditions (1.15-1.75 V vs RHE) shows Fe-O at 752 cm⁻¹ weakening with red shift below 1.35 V, then NiFeOOH formation with peaks at 472 cm⁻¹ and 559 cm⁻¹ at 1.45 V.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At potentials below 1.35 V, the spectrum is dominated by a broad band at 752 cm⁻¹, attributed to Fe-O vibrations... At 1.45 V, new distinct peaks emerge at 472 and 559 cm⁻¹, corresponding to the bending and stretching vibrational modes of NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Non-Faradaic CV determines Cdl = 20.81 mF·cm⁻² for Ni-CoFe₂O₄/NF vs 8.72 mF·cm⁻² (Ni/NF) and 6.96 mF·cm⁻² (NF) for ECSA estimation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface area (ECSA), estimated from the double-layer capacitance (Cdl) extracted via non-Faradaic cyclic voltammetry (Figure 2d; Figure S30), shows that Ni-CoFe₂O₄/NF possesses a substantially larger Cdl (20.81 mF·cm⁻²) compared to Ni/NF (8.72 mF·cm⁻²) and bare NF (6.96 mF·cm⁻²).
